title: How to press and store a cross-stitch project
subtitle: Pressing finished stitching flat and keeping it in good condition between sessions
excerpt: Pressing a finished cross-stitch piece removes hoop marks, settles the stitches, and prepares the fabric for framing or finishing. The piece is pressed face down on a padded surface so the stitches are not flattened. Storing a piece correctly between sessions prevents fading, distortion, and dust build-up.
sourceNotes: Pressing and storage guidance for cross-stitch. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.
The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch.

content.text: Pressing a completed piece from the wrong side removes the hoop ring impression from the
and restores the fabric grain. Pressing from the front would flatten the
and remove the slight relief of the cross-stitch, so always press face down on a padded surface.

Place a clean, folded towel on a flat ironing surface. The towel provides a padded layer that protects the stitches from being crushed. A piece of felt or a dedicated embroidery pressing pad also works.
Lay the stitched piece face down on the towel, with the stitched surface against the terry cloth. The back of the Aida faces up.

Set the iron to a medium temperature suitable for the Aida fabric and the thread. Most standard DMC floss is cotton and will tolerate a medium-cotton iron setting. A damp pressing cloth laid over the back of the Aida adds steam without direct contact.

Press the iron onto the back of the fabric with light pressure. Do not drag the iron across the work; lift and place it rather than sliding. Work outward from the centre to the edges so that any distortion is pressed to the margins rather than into the stitched area.
Allow the piece to cool flat before moving it. Moving hot, damp Aida can re-distort it. The fabric should be smooth and the stitches should have a clear relief once it is cool and set.

To store between sessions, roll the piece loosely around a clean card tube, stitched side out. Never fold a piece in progress; a fold crease in Aida is difficult to remove, especially in the stitched area. Store in a clean cotton bag or pillowcase away from direct light and damp.

items.symptom: Hoop marks remain visible after pressing
items.cause: The fabric was not damp enough during pressing, or the iron temperature was too low.
items.fix: Dampen the back of the Aida with a spray of clean water and press again with a slightly higher temperature. If the ring mark is deep, wet the fabric thoroughly, pin it out to shape on a blocking board, and allow it to dry flat rather than pressing.

items.symptom: The stitches look flat after pressing
items.cause: The piece was pressed face down on a hard surface rather than a padded one, or the iron was dragged rather than lifted.
items.fix: You cannot restore crushed stitches by pressing again. For future pieces, always use a thick padded surface and lift the iron rather than sliding it. The stitches should retain a clear relief if the pressing cloth absorbs the pressure.

content.text: Pressing is the final step before a piece is mounted or framed. A well-pressed piece with clean margins mounts more easily than one with hoop marks or distortion, and a framer can work with it immediately. Allow the piece to cool before presenting it to a framer, as a piece that is still warm from pressing can stretch when handled.
